newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.5 point to 14.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cuts rate 0.5 point to 14.7 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday it was lowering its key lending rate for January by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.7 percent.
The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly monetary tenders.

The central bank said in a statement its decision to lower rates, after holding them at 15.2 percent for the two previous months, reflected positive developments in inflation, inflationary expectations in the bond market and in the money supply.

The bank warned, however, that inflationary expectations were at the top of the 1997 inflation target of seven to 10 percent and that under the circumstances it had to maintain a cautious policy on interest rates.

It stressed the importance of the government's keeping the 1997 budget deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. It said the deficit goal should be met via spending cuts and not through new taxes.
Israel's financial markets had been predicting that the central bank would lower interest rates between 0.3 and 0.5 percentage points.
Inflation has fallen in the second half of the year and in the bond market inflationary expectations for the coming 12 months are now running at about 9.8 percent.

The Bank of Israel's decision comes as the Treasury is seeking to win parliament's approval for its 1997 budget. On Sunday, the finance committee approved the Arrangements Law that spells out the legislative changes accompanying the budget.

Analysts said on Monday that the Treasury's deficit projections for next year may not be met because of lower tax revenues than forecast. In announcing the rate cut, the Bank of Israel said it estimated the government's December deficit was especially big.
